newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai ended mixed on Thursday with turnover rising to 12.67 million lots from 11.61 million.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract fell to 21.00 percent from 24.50 percent on Wednesday and the seven-day contract edged up to 14.32 percent from 14.00.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said the fall in the three-day contract was a technical correction after several days of rises. "But rates for early-maturing contracts are still high because an active stock market is sucking money out of the repo market," said a trader.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai closed mostly down with liquidity flowing into the more active stock market, traders said. Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 3.54 million lots from 2.58 million due to institutional selling, they said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 ended down at 121.33 yuan from 121.87 yuan.

"Many investors were eager to cash in their positions today to speculate on the stock market," said one trader. "This resulted in falls today. Many investors believe the spot market will not rally in the near term." - Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004.
